title: Open external tensor coherence for whole semilinear systems
statement:
Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be a strict inverse sequence of commutative rings. For each scheme $Z$ use a small skeleton of $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the category $\mathscr S_Z$ of strict semilinear systems of $(C_n)_Z$-module sheaves: transitions are linear along $C_{n+1}\to C_n$ and morphisms commute with transitions. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, simultaneous exact inverse images $P_v$, total derived direct images $S_v$, $P_v\dashv S_v$, and derived tensor over the ring system $((C_n)_Z)_n$, with the canonical tensor, composition, unit and counit maps [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For an open immersion $j$ use exact $J_j\dashv P_j$ with identity open unit and the normalized open base-change and tensor maps $\beta,\gamma$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].
Let $\bar X\to B$, $\bar Y\to B$, $\bar W\to B$ be morphisms of schemes, and $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$, $l:W\hookrightarrow\bar W$ open immersions. Put $T=X\times_BY$, $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $u=j\times_Bk$, with projections $p,q$ and $\bar p,\bar q$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For arbitrary $K_\bullet\in D(\mathscr S_X)$, $L_\bullet\in D(\mathscr S_Y)$ set $D=P_pK_\bullet\otimes^LP_qL_\bullet$ and $V=P_{\bar p}J_jK_\bullet\otimes^LP_{\bar q}J_kL_\bullet$. Define $e_{j,k}:V\to J_uD$ by the ordered word: factor $u=j_1k_1$ through $X\times_B\bar Y$, apply $\beta$ for $j$, then $\gamma$ for $j_1$, then inside $J_{j_1}$ apply $\beta$ for $k$ and $\gamma$ for $k_1$ with signed symmetry placing its extension factor first, and finally the canonical open compositor $J_{j_1}J_{k_1}\cong J_u$.
This word is a natural isomorphism in the derived system category, preserves all coefficient actions and transitions, and $P_ue_{j,k}=1_D$ under the open units. The word through $\bar X\times_BY$ gives the same map. Transporting the reversed-factor word along the product swap gives $\widetilde e_{k,j}$, and
$$e_{j,k}=J_u(\sigma)\,\widetilde e_{k,j}\,\sigma.$$
For arbitrary $M_\bullet\in D(\mathscr S_W)$ the two iterated words $e_{j\times k,l}(e_{j,k}\boxtimes1)$ and $e_{j,k\times l}(1\boxtimes e_{k,l})$, including open compositors and tensor associators, are equal on the triple product and restrict to its canonical tensor associator. These are identities before finite evaluation or scalar restriction. No normalization, flatness of coefficient transitions, boundedness, constructibility or properness is assumed.

proof.text: Work throughout in the ordinary derived category of whole semilinear systems. The diagram-site clause of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] applies with ring system $((C_n)_Z)_n$: it gives natural invertible $\beta,\gamma$, invertible open units, and fully faithful $J_v$ for every open $v$. The system operations and their naturality are supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Thus every operation and comparison below is a morphism of systems, not a chosen family of evaluated arrows. For composable opens $a,b$, the unit of $J_aJ_b\dashv P_bP_a$ is $P_b(\eta^a_{J_bF})\eta^b_F$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The unique-left-adjoint comparison $c_{a,b}:J_aJ_b\cong J_{ab}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore satisfies $P_{ab}(c_{a,b})P_b(\eta^a_{J_bF})\eta^b_F=\eta^{ab}_F$ under pullback composition. Hence its restriction is the identity under these unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-derived diagram-topos external-product coherence argument using the normalized maps of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization.

proof.text: Write $A=X\times_B\bar Y$, $a=j_1:A\hookrightarrow\bar T$, $b=k_1:T\hookrightarrow A$, and let $r:A\to X$, $s:A\to\bar Y$ be the projections. Set $F=P_rK_\bullet$ and $H=P_sJ_kL_\bullet$. Open base change for $j$ turns $V$ into $J_aF\otimes^LP_{\bar q}J_kL_\bullet$. Applying $\gamma^a$ turns this into $J_a(F\otimes^LH)$. Open base change for $k$ gives $\delta:H\xrightarrow{\sim}J_bP_qL_\bullet$. Inside $J_a$, use $1\otimes\delta$, then $\sigma$, then $\gamma^b$, then $J_b(\sigma)$, obtaining $J_aJ_b(P_bF\otimes^LP_qL_\bullet)$. Pullback composition identifies $P_bF=P_pK_\bullet$; finish with $c_{a,b}$. This is exactly the specified ordered word. Every factor is natural and invertible by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], the system functoriality of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], and step 1. It gives a natural system isomorphism $e:V\xrightarrow{\sim}J_uD$.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-derived diagram-topos external-product coherence argument using the normalized maps of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization.

proof.text: Let $r_u:P_uV\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ be restriction/tensor comparison followed by the inverse open units of $j,k$. Restrict the word of step 2 along $u=ab$. Each $\beta$ becomes the identity under pullback composition and the corresponding open units; each $\gamma$ becomes the identity under restriction/tensor comparison, by the explicit restriction clauses of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The two symmetries surrounding $\gamma^b$ become $\sigma_{P_qL,P_pK}\sigma_{P_pK,P_qL}=1$, the symmetry identity of the derived tensor on the ringed diagram site [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. On homogeneous tensor terms their signs multiply to $(-1)^{ij+ji}=1$. The last compositor satisfies the unit equation of step 1. Consequently $P_ue=\eta^u_Dr_u$, equivalently $P_ue=1_D$ with the stated identifications. These computations use the canonical system comparisons of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], so take place before evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-derived diagram-topos external-product coherence argument using the normalized maps of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization.

proof.text: Restriction is injective on maps from this particular $V$ to $J_uD'$. Indeed, precompose a pair of such maps with $e^{-1}$ to get maps $h,h':J_uD\to J_uD'$. Fullness of $J_u$ writes them $J_u(t),J_u(t')$. Naturality of its invertible unit gives $P_uJ_u(t)=\eta^u_{D'}t(\eta^u_D)^{-1}$, and likewise for $t'$. Equality after restriction implies $t=t'$, hence $h=h'$ and the original maps agree. This uses only the full faithfulness and unit of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]; it makes no assertion about restriction on arbitrary ambient sources.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-derived diagram-topos external-product coherence argument using the normalized maps of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization.

proof.text: Repeat steps 2--3 with $X,Y$ interchanged, or equivalently use the factorization through $\bar X\times_BY$: the same normalized $\beta,\gamma$ give an isomorphism with the same source and target and restriction $\eta^u_Dr_u$. Step 4 proves it equals $e$. For the swapped-factor word, transport along the product swap and insert the input and output symmetries as in the statement. Naturality of the canonical tensor and pullback comparisons identifies its restriction with $\eta^u_D\sigma_{P_qL,P_pK}\sigma_{P_pK,P_qL}r_u=\eta^u_Dr_u$. The signs cancel as in step 3, by $\sigma_{L,K}\sigma_{K,L}=1$ [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Step 4 therefore gives $e_{j,k}=J_u(\sigma)\widetilde e_{k,j}\sigma$, with the Koszul signs included.

proof.text: On the triple product put $v=j\times k\times l$, $H_3=J_jK\boxtimes J_kL\boxtimes J_lM$ and $D_3=K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$, with a fixed parenthesization. Form the two iterated words using step 2. Functoriality preserves their invertibility. Restrict along $v$. For the left word the first comparison restricts to $1_{K\boxtimes L}\boxtimes1_M$ by step 3 and the second to $1_{D_3}$; for the right word they restrict to $1_K\boxtimes1_{L\boxtimes M}$ and $1_{D_3}$. The open compositors contribute the composite unit of step 1. The remaining tensor comparison is in both cases the canonical associator of the symmetric monoidal derived tensor [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]: on total tensor representatives it is $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, with no sign. Restriction carries each of these tensor sections to the same section. This is an identity on complexes on the diagram site; the tensor localization of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and the total-complex convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] carry it to the derived system category. Thus, after the stated associators, both restrictions equal $1_{D_3}$.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent-derived diagram-topos external-product coherence argument using the normalized maps of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization.

proof.text: One of the iterated words identifies $H_3$ with $J_vD_3$. Apply the three-line argument of step 4 with this isomorphism and $v$ in place of $e$ and $u$. The equal restrictions of step 6 imply equality of the two iterated words. Every construction was made in the whole system category and hence preserves coefficient actions and transitions. All inputs to the normalization theorem were arbitrary unbounded complexes over arbitrary ring systems; no flat transition, cartesian-system, constructibility or properness hypothesis entered the argument.
